craft_notes: Sthāyin: twoness collapsed — the plunge clause. Sanskrit-first: punar api (again-too) kept the re-entry; bahir-antar-tas kept outer-inner as one adverb; tanmayīkṛte (made-of-That) kept as predicate; nimajjanam kept plunging (not bathing-word). Rows: 9 (outer/inner pair named then collapsed), 1 (‘thus told’ closes — uktaṃ verdict-voice), 6 (iti anchors). Close: 'plunging here, there: thus told.' Rejected: 'immersion' for nimajjanam — killed: ni-√majj is plunge, distinct from samāveśa used earlier; 'made by That' — killed: tanmayīkṛta is made-OF-That (identity, not agency). Read aloud: A-gain-TOO, AS-OUT-er-IN-ner-TWO-ness: BY-one-ness WITH the-OUT-ward-WOR-shipped-MAN-tra, MADE of-THAT — PLUNG-ing HERE, THERE: THUS-told.

lines: by oneness with the outward-worshipped mantra,
made of That — plunging here, there: thus told.
l4.sanskrit_cite: punar api bāhyābhyantaratayā dvitvam bahirupāsyamantratādātmyena tanmayīkṛte tatra tatra nimajjanam ity uktam

reads_against.argmap: What is the outer-inner twoness of the plunge? → The twoness of bāhya/ābhyantara is collapsed by mantra-tādātmya: made-of-That, the plunge here-there is pronounced and closed.
c1_essence: Outer-inner twoness collapses by oneness with the outward-worshipped mantra: made-of-That, plunging here-there, thus told.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta with vidhi weight (quiescence carrying ritual order)
